content: Healthcare providers are encouraged to adopt a communication style that is centered on the individual patient, culturally sensitive, and focused on leveraging the patient’s strengths. This approach involves actively listening to the patient, respecting their personal preferences and beliefs, and taking into account their health literacy and numeracy skills. The goal of this method is to optimize both the patient’s health outcomes and their overall quality of life. By employing this approach, providers can more effectively understand and address the unique needs and expectations of each patient, which is particularly critical in the management of chronic conditions such as diabetes. Individuals with diabetes can benefit significantly from a well-coordinated, interprofessional care team. Such a team may include, but is not limited to, diabetes care and education specialists, nurses, registered dietitian nutritionists, exercise specialists, pharmacists, dentists, podiatrists, and behavioral health professionals. The inclusion of diverse expertise within the care team ensures that all aspects of diabetes management are comprehensively addressed, ranging from dietary guidance to mental health support.
